news.title: Valid certificates, stolen accounts: how attackers broke npm's last trust signal
news.summary_raw: On May 19, 633 malicious npm package versions passed Sigstore provenance verification. They were cleared by the system because the attacker had generated valid signing certificates from a compromised maintainer account.Sigstore worked exactly as designed: it verified the package was built in a CI environment, confirmed a valid certificate was issued, and recorded everything in the transparency log. What it cannot do is determine whether the person holding the credentials authorized the publish —
news.summary: Attackers compromised a maintainer account on npm, generating valid signing certificates and bypassing Sigstore's provenance verification. This highlights a vulnerability in Sigstore's design, where it cannot determine if the person holding the credentials authorized the publication.
news.enterprise_use: Check your organization's npm package management and CI/CD pipeline security, as a compromised maintainer account can generate valid certificates and bypass trust signals. Missing this means exposing your organization to potential security risks from malicious packages. Review your team's npm configuration and consider implementing additional security measures, such as multi-factor authentication for maintainer accounts.
